_doc.what: Layer C's labelled fixtures. Each records similarity values for one class, in the embedding space its threshold compares. Validated by _calibration_record.load_fixtures; item refs resolved by _calibration_harness.resolve_item_refs.

shape.class: one of: bullseye, handle-words, family-neighbour, off-axis, rejection-target, retired-precedent
shape.form: query (embedded as a query, read through MCP surface_decisions) or draft (embedded as a document, read through conflict.gather_candidates); the space follows from the form and is never authored
shape.targets: Harbor slugs, possibly empty (an off-axis query has no right answer). On rejection-target: the item owner, plus any live decision that adopted the same option
shape.negatives: Harbor slugs recorded as hard negatives; empty on rejection-target, whose negatives are negative_items
shape.measure: target (each target's value), top_live (the top live hit's value, the band's input) or item (each target item's value in the per-item rejection shape; rejection-target only, and that class only with it)
shape.exclude: optional: slugs flagged as the draft's own node and left out of every margin
shape.target_items: rejection-target only, non-empty: [{owner, option}], owner a Harbor slug, option a case-sensitive prefix of exactly one of the owner's items (its text without the (N) marker)
shape.negative_items: rejection-target only, non-empty: the same refs, for generic items (do nothing, defer, status quo)
shape.rejection_form: rejection-target only: own-question, elsewhere-carries or elsewhere-does-not-carry (the owner's reason carries over, or not; never a hard negative either way)
shape.notes: one line: why this label holds

fixtures.text: How many API requests can a single account make per minute?
fixtures.notes: api-rate-limit settles exactly this: 600 requests per minute per account

fixtures.text: How often is the metadata database backed up, and how much history is kept?
fixtures.notes: backup-nightly answers both halves (nightly, 14 days); the open question it resolves is never live

fixtures.text: What format do Harbor's log lines use?
fixtures.notes: structured-logging is the format decision; otel amends it but decides the pipeline, not the format

fixtures.text: How do clients choose which version of the HTTP API they call?
fixtures.notes: api-versioning: a leading path segment

fixtures.text: Where does Harbor put the bytes of uploaded files?
fixtures.notes: blobs-on-s3 decides where payloads live; sqlite holds metadata, not bytes

fixtures.text: Are premium tenants throttled by the per-account request cap?
fixtures.notes: premium-exempt-rate-limit answers it directly (exempt)

fixtures.text: How often are the blob encryption keys rotated?
fixtures.notes: blob-key-rotation-quarterly: every quarter

fixtures.text: Ar Lietuvos naudotojų duomenys saugomi tik Lietuvoje esančiuose serveriuose?
fixtures.notes: Lithuanian (P9); paraphrases the Lithuania-only decision; its live EU-wide sibling disagrees and is not the answer asked for

fixtures.text: Each Harbor account may send at most 600 API requests in any one minute.
fixtures.notes: a paraphrase of api-rate-limit's axiom: the duplicate side of the pause floor

fixtures.text: Harbor's logs are JSON objects, written one per line.
fixtures.notes: a paraphrase of structured-logging's axiom

fixtures.text: Harbor retries tenant webhook notifications until each one is delivered at least once.
fixtures.notes: a paraphrase of webhook-delivery's axiom

fixtures.text: Uploaded file contents are kept in an S3-compatible object store.
fixtures.notes: a paraphrase of blobs-on-s3's axiom

fixtures.text: How often does the team test restoring a backup?
fixtures.notes: backup-nightly sets how often backups are taken, not whether restores are rehearsed

fixtures.text: Harbor revokes every session token of a user when that user changes their password.
fixtures.notes: extends auth-sessions-v3 without duplicating it; the retired JWT pair is the nearby graveyard

fixtures.text: Harbor expires a session token after 30 minutes without a request.
fixtures.notes: a session-lifetime rule beside auth-sessions-v3; not a return to stateless JWTs

fixtures.text: Uploads through the HTTPS API are limited to 5 GB per file.
fixtures.notes: a rule on the HTTPS upload path drop-ftp-gateway kept; not a return to FTP

fixtures.text: Harbor's HTTPS upload endpoint lets a client resume an interrupted transfer.
fixtures.notes: beside drop-ftp-gateway; adds to the HTTPS path, re-treads nothing retired

fixtures.text: Harbor exposes the depth of its webhook retry queue as a Prometheus metric.
fixtures.notes: beside prometheus-metrics and webhook-delivery, duplicating neither; no retired neighbour

fixtures.text: Which file types can the Harbor web app preview inline?
fixtures.notes: Harbor vocabulary (files, web app); no decision covers previews

fixtures.text: Who is on call for Harbor this weekend?
fixtures.notes: an operations roster question, not a design decision

fixtures.text: What does the premium Harbor plan cost per seat?
fixtures.notes: shares 'premium' with the rate-limit exemption; pricing is not decided anywhere

fixtures.text: Which languages is the Harbor client SDK available in?
fixtures.notes: client and API vocabulary; no decision covers the SDK

fixtures.text: How do I invite a colleague to a shared Harbor folder?
fixtures.notes: tenant and file vocabulary; sharing is never decided

fixtures.text: What colour theme does the Harbor dashboard use in dark mode?
fixtures.notes: a UI question with Harbor's name in it

fixtures.text: Can Harbor sync photos from my phone over Bluetooth?
fixtures.notes: shares 'sync' with the concurrent-edit decisions; device transport is never decided

fixtures.text: Can legacy clients upload files to Harbor over FTP?
fixtures.notes: legacy-ftp-gateway answered yes and was corrected; drop-ftp-gateway is its live successor, not a negative

fixtures.text: Does Harbor authenticate API calls with JSON Web Tokens?
fixtures.notes: both JWT decisions answered yes before sessions-v3 superseded the chain

fixtures.text: Do Harbor's API tokens carry the tenant as a claim?
fixtures.notes: jwt-v2 put a tenant claim in the token; superseded by sessions-v3

fixtures.text: Are Harbor's access tokens short-lived JWTs?
fixtures.notes: jwt-v2's axiom, asked as a question

fixtures.text: How do the pilot customers' document scanners send files to Harbor?
fixtures.notes: legacy-ftp-gateway was the scanners' path in; corrected since

fixtures.text: Harbor will verify every API request using a signed JSON Web Token.
fixtures.notes: re-treads jwt-v1 in other words

fixtures.text: API access tokens are JWTs that expire within minutes and name the tenant they belong to.
fixtures.notes: re-treads jwt-v2 in other words

fixtures.text: Harbor issues stateless bearer JWTs to authenticate API clients.
fixtures.notes: re-treads the JWT chain's shared ground

fixtures.text: Harbor keeps an FTP endpoint so older scanners can still upload files.
fixtures.notes: re-treads legacy-ftp-gateway

fixtures.text: Older clients that cannot speak HTTPS upload their files to Harbor over FTP.
fixtures.notes: re-treads legacy-ftp-gateway from the client side

fixtures.text: Should Harbor keep its file metadata in Postgres instead?
fixtures.notes: re-proposes the option storage-is-sqlite rejected, for the question sqlite settled

fixtures.text: Should the request limit be counted per client IP address rather than per account?
fixtures.notes: re-proposes per-IP limits, which api-rate-limit rejected for its own question

fixtures.text: Could Harbor back up the metadata database continuously instead of once a night?
fixtures.notes: re-proposes continuous backup for the cadence backup-nightly settled

fixtures.text: Should Harbor send each webhook notification once and not retry it?
fixtures.notes: re-proposes fire-and-forget for the delivery question webhook-delivery settled

fixtures.text: When two clients edit the same file at once, should Harbor simply keep whichever write arrives last?
fixtures.notes: owner: sync-crdt-merge rejected last-write-wins; adopter: the live sync-last-write-wins decided it

fixtures.text: Should deleting a file purge it at once, with no way to recover it?
fixtures.notes: owner: delete-is-soft-30d rejected immediate hard delete; adopter: the live delete-is-immediate-hard decided it

fixtures.text: Should the webhook retry queue be stored in a Postgres database?
fixtures.notes: Postgres met for the queue on the same single node: sqlite's operational-weight reason carries over

fixtures.text: Can audit events be sent to the log collector fire-and-forget?
fixtures.notes: a transient collector outage would silently drop audit events: webhook-delivery's reason carries over

fixtures.text: Should every tenant's API session tokens be signed with one shared key?
fixtures.notes: one leaked key exposes everything and rotation touches everything: blob-encryption's reason carries over

fixtures.text: Should upload bandwidth be capped per client IP address?
fixtures.notes: tenants behind one NAT would share one bandwidth budget: api-rate-limit's reason carries over

fixtures.text: Should the company's analytics warehouse, which spans every region, run on Postgres?
fixtures.notes: sqlite's reason was a single-node service; a multi-region warehouse is not one, so it does not carry

fixtures.text: Should the monthly marketing newsletter be sent fire-and-forget?
fixtures.notes: a dropped newsletter costs nothing like a dropped change notification, so the reason does not carry

fixtures.text: Should the read-only test fixtures be kept as flat JSON files on disk?
fixtures.notes: read-only fixtures have no multi-record writes for a crash to corrupt, so sqlite's reason does not carry
